claims.claim: Musical form is the organization of musical elements in time, or the sections or movements of a piece.
Memory enables listeners to recognize repetition, contrast, and variation, which provide structure and shape in musical form.
A common introductory convention uses alphabetic labels for sections: returning material repeats the letter, allowing layouts such as AB and ABA to represent binary and ternary forms.
In the cited LOUIS description of popular song forms, a chorus or refrain normally uses recurring lyrics and music within a song, while a verse is generally heard once, though not always.
Letter labels are analytical shorthand for relationships among sections rather than inherent grades of importance or proof that every section is exactly identical.
A careful listener identifies returns and contrasts in the audible music before choosing a formal label, and avoids forcing a single introductory Western label on every musical practice.
